title: Candy Corn Bag

adjustment.analysis: No events, promotions, or price changes in the target week. Recent weeks show no sustained trend beyond seasonal noise. The baseline already captures back-to-school seasonality, and Labor Day (2026-09-07) had a 10% discount with a 1.75x lift, but that was a one-off event with a 1.08x lift in the following week—no evidence of lasting demand shift. The classical uplift model correctly finds no driver. Noise-adjusted promotion effects are modest (x1.48), and the product's ordinary week noise is ±80%, so no adjustment is justified.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 14.5 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 28.3 | 10%-90%: 4.6 - 24.1

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-80% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
